# Independent audit: one-coordinate facet-roof extraction

Audited source: all-dimensional-one-coordinate-facet-roof-extraction-root.md.
Audited and rerun verifier: verify_all_dimensional_one_coordinate_facet_roof_root.py.


passes 3039 exact hinge, curvature-mixture, and normalization checks. The
all-dimensional conclusions below follow from the proof, rather than
from the verifier's finite dimension range.

## 1. Conditional multiplicity and hinge deficit

The normalized facet marginal is
\((d-1)(1-x)^{d-2}\). Conditioning on \(s_1=x\), each remaining
coordinate contributes the tail of a scaled \((d-2)\)-simplex.
This gives the displayed density-weighted multiplicity exactly.
For \(d=2\), the remaining coordinate is deterministic; the source
correctly replaces the last truncated zeroth power by
\(\mathbf 1_{\{x<h\}}\). Its value at \(h\) is immaterial.

The functional kills affine functions: symmetry gives
\(\mathbb E[Ns_i]=\mathbb E[N]/d\), while
\(\mathbb E[N]=d h^{d-1}=m\Gamma\). The three hinge integrals and
their signs in (2) consequently check. Direct differentiation gives
the stated \(I_L\), including the \(c>L\) branch.

For \(0\le c\le b\), the ratio \((h-c)/(1-c)\) is at most \(h\);
the lower bound in (5) follows from
\(dh-(d-1)=1/m\). It remains valid when \(d-2=0\).
Together with the two zero initial conditions it gives strict
positivity on \((0,b]\). On \([b,1)\), formula (4) divided by
\((1-c)^d\) is nondecreasing and begins strictly positive.
This proves positivity for every dimension and every interior hinge.

In particular,
\[
k_2=\frac{dE(b)}{h^d}
=d h^{d-1}-1-(d-1)((d-1)/d)^d>0.
\]
No extra numerical bound for \(k_2\) is being assumed.

## 2. Majorants and possibly infinite curvature

For \(c\le b\), the constant majorant has error
\((d-1)I_1(c)\); integrating the second-derivative comparison
twice gives the claimed factor \(k_1\). For \(c\ge b\), the
majorant \(x\) has error \((1-c)^d/d\); the monotone ratio from
Section 1 gives factor \(k_2\). Thus one common \(k_d\) applies
to every hinge.

The Green representation is valid for an arbitrary continuous
concave function with finite endpoint values, even when its curvature
measure has infinite total mass. In particular it has
\[
\int_0^b c\,d\mu(c)<\infty,\qquad
\int_b^1(1-c)\,d\mu(c)<\infty.
\]
One direct endpoint justification is that concavity and continuity
imply \(x\phi'_+(x)\to0\) at zero and the analogous limit at one;
integration by parts on compact interior intervals gives these
weighted integrability statements and the Green representation.
Equivalently, its value at a fixed interior point controls the two
weighted integrals.

These are precisely the weights needed to integrate the chosen
affine majorants. The resulting affine function is finite and
majorizes the roof, with nonnegative endpoint values. The signed
deficit interchange is absolutely integrable: the Green mixture is
nonnegative with finite integral, and \(N-m\Gamma\) is bounded.
The majorant-error interchange is Tonelli for a nonnegative
integrand. Thus the proof does not silently assume finite total
curvature or bounded endpoint slopes. Strict positivity of every
interior hinge deficit gives the stated affine equality case.

## 3. Actual body, Jacobian, and maximum-depth normalization

The displayed coordinate map to the standard simplex has determinant
one. Uniform facet probability agrees with uniform probability in
the coordinate simplex; the Euclidean facet-area factor cancels
when normalized. Vertical added volume uses the coordinate base
volume \(1/(d-1)!=dV\), as in the source.

The roof body is convex, contains the original simplex, and has exact
added volume
\(\epsilon dV\int\phi\,dP\).
Its normalized added law converges to the stated bounded-density
facet law. The canonical centroid hyperplane opposite this facet
misses it, and the other canonical hyperplanes have proper
codimension-one traces. All have zero limit-law mass, as required
by the separately audited weak-added-law first-variation theorem.

Writing the first-order canonical average before normalizing gives
\[
\epsilon d\left[
\frac1m\int N\phi\,dP-\Gamma\int\phi\,dP
\right]
=\epsilon\frac d m E_d(\phi).
\]
This verifies both the Jacobian and the subtraction of the added
total mass. The cited theorem supplies an attained maximum and the
all-direction estimate; the source does not substitute canonical
upper bounds for an all-direction lower bound.

## 4. Enclosing simplex and the extraction ratio

For \(\ell=A+Bx\), the majorant construction gives \(A\ge0\) and
\(A+B\ge0\). With \(q=r-\sum z_j+1\), the proposed enclosure is
exactly the simplex
\[
q+(1-\epsilon B)z_1+\sum_{j\ge2}z_j\le1+\epsilon A,
\qquad q,z_j\ge0.
\]
Its volume is therefore exactly
\[
V\frac{(1+\epsilon A)^d}{1-\epsilon B}.
\]
Since \(\int\ell\,dP=A+B/d\), its first-order excess over the
actual roof body is \(\epsilon dV\int(\ell-\phi)\,dP\).
The remaining volume is \(O_\phi(\epsilon^2)\) by expansion of
this exact formula. There is no omitted first-order contribution
from outside the original coordinate projection.

For nonaffine \(\phi\), the error integral is strictly positive:
otherwise the nonnegative continuous difference \(\ell-\phi\)
would vanish identically. Dividing the two first-order expressions
therefore gives the claimed lower ratio \(k_d/m\).
For nested uniform laws the supremum-set total variation is the
relative missing volume; halfspace distance is no larger. Replacing
the denominator by its infimum over affine simplices can only
strengthen the lower ratio while the numerator is positive.

The fixed-roof qualification is essential and is retained:
no uniform remainder for roofs depending on \(\epsilon\) is claimed.
The affine case is explicitly separated. The result remains an
ordinary one-coordinate facet-roof statement, with no assertion
about general facet roofs or mixed OC.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
